summary: Biography of Heinrich Himmler, a Munich-born former schoolboy steeped in völkisch occultism who rose through the Nazi Party to lead the SS from 1929, building it into a racial order that ran Germany's police and concentration camps.

evidence.note: Himmler born October 1900 in Munich to an upper-middle-class Bavarian family
joins Röhm's Freikorps unit and then the NSDAP around 1922-23
becomes Reichsführer-SS after the previous leader is ousted
series narrative stops around the outbreak of WWII and the early war years
long segment on Lanz von Liebenfels, born 1874 in Vienna, and his New Templars
Liebenfels buys Werfenstein castle in Austria as his order's headquarters
extended segment on Wiligut, his Irminist visions and asylum committal
Himmler's Mein Kampf notes on undoing racial mixing; SS as a breeding project
Himmler models the SS on occult secret societies and the Knights Templar
protective custody, Dachau handed to the SS, Himmler takes over state police forces
host reads out Liebenfels's race-war propaganda at length

notes: Series ends around 1939-41; covered_span.end is 1945 only because of the lifetime rule. covered_span.start 1888 is an estimate for the List/Liebenfels background segments (secondary subjects). main_span starts with joining the NSDAP/Beer Hall Putsch, although childhood is a large share. Ernst Röhm also gets a big segment but the subject cap was reached. No role fits a party paramilitary chief well.
